title: The Service Layer
blurb: Business logic lives here, not in the controller. This is the hub for the judgment-flavored puzzles — deferred LINQ execution and async pitfalls that have one right answer once you know the rule.

levels.title: L1 · Deferred execution
levels.prompt: LINQ queries are lazy. What does r contain?

blocks.label: Code

failStates.title: The query runs at ToList(), not at Where()
failStates.explain: Where() only describes the query. It actually executes at ToList() — which happens AFTER Add(4). So the source is {1,2,3,4} and both 3 and 4 pass the >2 filter.

failStates.title: It's deferred, not broken
failStates.explain: Deferred execution means q re-reads the (now updated) list when ToList() runs. The result is [3, 4], not empty.

levels.title: L2 · The blocking .Result deadlock
levels.prompt: This can deadlock in a request context. Find the offending line and pick the fix.

payload.intro: Blocking on an async call with .Result (or .Wait()) while a synchronization context is captured is the classic deadlock.

nodes.label: var data = FetchAsync().Result;
nodes.sub: blocks the thread waiting on the task

fixes.label: await FetchAsync() and make the calling method async all the way up

failStates.title: The async method is fine
failStates.explain: FetchAsync() is a normal async method. The bug is blocking on it with .Result, which can deadlock when the awaited continuation needs the thread you're blocking.

failStates.title: Using the data is fine
failStates.explain: Consuming the result isn't the problem — it's how the result was obtained: a blocking .Result instead of an await.

failStates.title: Task.Run hides it, wastes a thread
failStates.explain: Offloading to a thread-pool thread dodges the captured context but burns a thread and treats the symptom. Async-all-the-way (await) is the real fix.

failStates.title: You're still blocking
failStates.explain: ConfigureAwait(false) is about the continuation context, but .Result still synchronously blocks. The fix is to await instead of block.
